lessons.title: Ancient Egypt: the gift of the Nile
lessons.programRef: Cameroon anglophone secondary History syllabus, Form 1 — to be checked against the official text
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Explain why the Nile was important to Egypt
Describe the pharaoh, society and religion
Describe the achievements of the ancient Egyptians
Explain how we know about ancient Egypt
reviewNotes: Teacher to verify: the approximate age of the pyramids (about 4500 years), the Rosetta Stone discovery (1799) and decipherment (1820s), and the wording about Herodotus.

Draft for teacher review: only well-established facts are used and the tone is neutral; every date and name must be verified against the official History syllabus and standard references before release.

blocks.md: Ancient Egypt grew along the **River Nile** in north-east Africa, in a land that is otherwise desert. Each year the river **flooded**, leaving rich black silt on its banks. Farmers grew wheat, barley and flax. The Greek writer Herodotus called Egypt the **'gift of the Nile'**. The river was also a highway for boats and carried stone for building.

blocks.caption: Egypt and the Nile
blocks.alt: A schematic map showing the Nile flowing north through desert to the sea with fertile land along its banks.

blocks.title: Government and society
blocks.md: The ruler of Egypt was the **pharaoh**, seen as a god-king, who owned the land and led the army and religion. Below him were **nobles and priests**, **officials and scribes** (who wrote records), **soldiers**, **craftworkers and merchants**, and a large number of **farmers** and workers. Egyptians worshipped many gods and believed in life after death.

blocks.title: Achievements
blocks.md:
- **Writing**: hieroglyphs on stone and, on **papyrus** (a paper made from a reed).
- **Building**: the **pyramids**, tombs of pharaohs, built about 4500 years ago, and great temples.
- **Science**: a calendar of 365 days, mathematics for measuring land, medicine, and **mummification**.
- **Art**: painting, sculpture, jewellery.

**How do we know?** Archaeologists have found tombs, paintings, statues and papyrus documents. The **Rosetta Stone**, found in 1799, had the same text in three scripts, which helped scholars to read hieroglyphs in the 1820s. Ancient Egypt influenced Greece and Rome, and also had links with other parts of Africa such as Nubia (Kush) to the south.

blocks.title: Be careful
blocks.md:
- Egypt is part of Africa, and the Egyptians were African people with links to other Africans.
- The pyramids were tombs, not just monuments.
- Egyptian civilisation lasted thousands of years; do not treat it as one short period.

blocks.title: Example 1: the Nile
blocks.statement: Explain why most Egyptians lived near the Nile.
steps: Most of Egypt is desert with very little rain.
The Nile gave water and the flood left fertile silt.
So people lived along the river.
blocks.answer: Because the river gave water and fertile land in a desert.

blocks.title: Example 2: writing
blocks.statement: Why was papyrus useful to the Egyptians?
steps: It was light and could be rolled and carried.
Scribes could keep records on it.
So government and trade could be recorded.
blocks.answer: It was a light writing material for records.
